title: Baking Spice Partial Acceptance
subject: Contracts
subtopic: UCC Article 2 - perfect tender buyer remedies
stem: Paul operates a baking-supply plant, and Rebekah owns a small cafe that buys ingredients for resale to local bakers. Paul ordinarily sells spice blends in cartons containing 12 tins per carton. By a valid written contract, Rebekah agreed to buy, and Paul agreed to sell, 10 cartons of Harvest Sage. When the cartons arrived, Rebekah inspected them and found that 2 cartons contained Citrus Thyme instead of Harvest Sage. Rebekah immediately notified Paul. Paul replied that he no longer produced Harvest Sage, had sent his last 8 cartons, and had included 2 cartons of Citrus Thyme as an accommodation. He added that Rebekah did not have to accept the Citrus Thyme unless she wanted it.
call: Which of the following correctly states Rebekah's rights regarding the shipment?

choices.A: Rebekah may accept the 8 cartons containing Harvest Sage and reject the 2 cartons containing Citrus Thyme, or accept the entire shipment and recover damages resulting from its nonconformity to the contract.
choices.B: Rebekah may reject the entire shipment, accept the 8 cartons containing Harvest Sage and reject the 2 cartons containing Citrus Thyme, or accept the entire shipment and recover damages resulting from its nonconformity to the contract.
choices.C: Rebekah may reject the entire shipment.
choices.D: Rebekah may reject the entire shipment, or accept the 8 cartons containing Harvest Sage and reject the 2 cartons containing Citrus Thyme.

rightExplanation: Under UCC section 2-601, a buyer receiving goods that fail in any respect to conform to the contract may reject the whole, accept the whole, or accept any commercial unit and reject the rest. Each carton is a commercial unit. If Rebekah accepts the entire nonconforming shipment, acceptance does not eliminate her damages remedy. Under UCC sections 2-607 and 2-714, she may recover damages resulting from the nonconformity. Paul's accommodation language does not narrow those remedies after a valid contract for conforming goods.

wrongExplanations.A: This choice offers two real remedies: partial acceptance of commercial units and acceptance with damages. Its pull is that both are expressly available under the UCC. The missing remedy is rejection of the entire nonconforming shipment.
wrongExplanations.C: Perfect tender makes rejection of the whole shipment available because the tender did not conform. The answer is incomplete because the UCC also permits acceptance of commercial units and acceptance of the whole with damages.
wrongExplanations.D: This is attractive because it preserves the two rejection paths: rejecting everything or accepting only conforming commercial units. The breaker is the omitted third path: Rebekah may accept the whole shipment and still claim damages for nonconformity.
